\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مبلمان} (moblemân)}{مبلمان (moblemân)}]{\fa{مبلمان} (moblemân) — furniture}

\label{lesson:FA-C534-mobleman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be broadcast, then the Persian for to stare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مبلمان}}
\textbf{\fa{مبلمان}} (\emph{moblemân}) — \textquotedblleft{}furniture\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آنها} \fa{برای} \fa{خانه} \fa{جدید} \fa{مبلمان} \fa{خریدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ânhâ barâ-ye khâne-ye jadid moblemân kharidand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They bought furniture for their new house.
\end{quote}

A collective noun; \emph{mobl} is one sofa or armchair.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{moblemân} was borrowed from French \emph{meublement}, 'furnishing' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{moblemân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{moblemân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{moblemân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be broadcast, then the Persian for to stare, then say \emph{moblemân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آباژور} (âbâzhur)}{آباژور (âbâzhur)}]{\fa{آباژور} (âbâzhur) — a lamp (with a shade); a lampshade}

\label{lesson:FA-C534-abazhur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stare, then the Persian for furniture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آباژور}}
\textbf{\fa{آباژور}} (\emph{âbâzhur}) — \textquotedblleft{}a lamp (with a shade); a lampshade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کنار} \fa{تخت} \fa{یک} \fa{آباژور} \fa{کوچک} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kenâr-e takht yek âbâzhur-e kuchek ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There's a small lamp beside the bed.
\end{quote}

A table or floor lamp with a shade.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âbâzhur} was borrowed from French \emph{abat-jour}, which EtymDB builds from \emph{abattre}, 'to throw down', and \emph{jour}, 'day, daylight', itself from Latin \emph{diurnum} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to stare, then the Persian for furniture, then say \emph{âbâzhur} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قالیچه} (qâliche)}{قالیچه (qâliche)}]{\fa{قالیچه} (qâliche) — a rug, a small carpet}

\label{lesson:FA-C534-qaliche}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for furniture, then the Persian for a lamp.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قالیچه}}
\textbf{\fa{قالیچه}} (\emph{qâliche}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rug, a small carpet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جلوی} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{قالیچه} \fa{قرمز} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jelo-ye dar yek qâliche-ye qermez ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There's a red rug in front of the door.
\end{quote}

\emph{qâli} 'carpet' + the diminutive \emph{-che}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qâliche} is built on \emph{qâli}, 'carpet', with the native diminutive \emph{-che}. EtymDB lists \emph{qâli} without a source, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کوسن} (kusan)}{کوسن (kusan)}]{\fa{کوسن} (kusan) — a cushion}

\label{lesson:FA-C534-kusan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a lamp, then the Persian for a rug.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کوسن}}
\textbf{\fa{کوسن}} (\emph{kusan}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cushion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{کوسنها} \fa{را} \fa{روی} \fa{مبل} \fa{چید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u kusanhâ râ ru-ye mobl chid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She arranged the cushions on the sofa.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{kusanhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kusan} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{coussin}, 'cushion'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لحاف} (lahâf)}{لحاف (lahâf)}]{\fa{لحاف} (lahâf) — a quilt, a duvet}

\label{lesson:FA-C534-lahaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rug, then the Persian for a cushion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لحاف}}
\textbf{\fa{لحاف}} (\emph{lahâf}) — \textquotedblleft{}a quilt, a duvet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{زمستان} \fa{زیر} \fa{لحاف} \fa{میخوابیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar zemestân zir-e lahâf mikhâbim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In winter we sleep under a quilt.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{lahâfhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lahâf} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{liḥāf}, 'a covering, a wrap'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
